ops.text:
ccx served pre-diff file content for a git worktree, so a code review nearly ran against the wrong bytes.

Hit 2026-08-19 reviewing an uncommitted change in `~/.claude/worktrees/daemonkit/wf_96107be7-dc3-3` (a worktree created by `Agent`/`Workflow` with `isolation: 'worktree'`). `ccx code read`/`symbol` against paths in that worktree returned the file as it was BEFORE the working-tree edits — the reviewing agent noticed the content didn't match `git diff`, abandoned ccx for that lane, and re-read everything with plain `cat`/`grep`. Its verdict was sound only because it caught the mismatch itself.

Why it matters more than a normal cache-staleness annoyance: the failure is silent and the output looks authoritative. An agent asked to review, verify, or refute a change in a worktree can be handed the pre-change bytes, find nothing wrong, and return a confident PASS on code it never actually read. That is a verification gate that reports green without having run. The same risk applies to any agent using ccx to check work in a worktree — including the adversarial-verify and finder/refuter lanes this fleet leans on.

Reproduce: create a worktree, edit a file in it without committing, then `ccx code read <worktree-path>/<file> --section N-M` and compare against `git -C <worktree> diff -- <file>`.

Workaround in use: when reviewing uncommitted changes in a worktree, read the diff with git and the files with cat/grep; do not trust ccx's view of a worktree path. Related: the sibling papercut about a concurrent `task lint` in a worktree poisoning the shared golangci-lint cache — both are worktree-vs-parent-checkout cache aliasing, and both fail in the direction of a misleading green.
